L01.text: If all the ice on Earth melted, the sea would rise about seventy meters. That's a twenty-storey building.

L02.text: Almost all of that ice sits in two places. Antarctica holds about ninety-one percent. Greenland, about eight.

L03.text: Every mountain glacier on the planet? Just one percent.

L04.text: Melt it, and the sea comes up the beach, over the boardwalk, and into town.

L05.text: First floor, gone. Fifth floor, gone. By the tenth floor, the fish are window shopping.

L06.text: Low countries vanish, and every coastline on the map gets redrawn.

L07.text: But here's the twist. The ice floating at the North Pole? Melt all of it, and the sea barely moves.

L08.text: Floating ice already pushes aside its own weight in water, just like an ice cube melting in a glass.

L09.text: It's the ice sitting on land that does the damage.

L10.text: Luckily, melting all of it would take thousands of years. Unluckily, the sea is already rising.

L11.text: So maybe skip the beach house, and buy the one on the hill.
